fatal_errors: The proposed comparison changes Cr/Al concentration rather than comparing as-printed and precipitation-aged states of the same alloy, so it cannot reveal the target role of Cr-depleted precipitates and matrix-precipitate interfaces.

The claim that inherent sluggish diffusion in multiprincipal-element alloys stabilizes the scale and matrix is unsupported by the cited evidence and is not the governing mechanism identified in the target.
Mechanical-property retention after oxidation is predicted without evidence connecting the proposed oxide-scale comparison to residual tensile or fracture behavior.
explanation: The hypothesis captures the broad principle that a continuous protective oxide, especially Cr2O3, suppresses inward oxygen and outward metal transport. It also proposes measurable oxidation kinetics and scale characterization over a partially overlapping temperature and duration range. However, it misses the central controlled comparison: identical SLM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 material in as-printed versus 750 °C/50 h aged states. Consequently, it does not reconstruct the L12/L21 precipitation, local Cr depletion, added interface pathways, delayed chromia formation, or the observed higher mass gain of the aged state with similar activation energies. Altering bulk Cr/Al creates a plausible generic alloy-design experiment but confounds chemistry with the microstructural mechanism of interest. E1 supports the general value of protective chromia but not the specific precipitation-mediated mechanism or sluggish-diffusion claim; E2 is largely irrelevant to oxidation-scale behavior.
